accepted.question_text: Let P(z) be a homogeneous polynomial of degree 4 in C[z] whose Hessian matrix Hes P is nilpotent, so P is Hessian nilpotent. If Delta := sum_{i=1}^n D_i^2 is the Laplace operator on C[z], must the iterated Laplacians of the powers of P eventually vanish in the sense that Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) = 0 for all sufficiently large m?
accepted.context_brief: vanishing conjecture for degree-4 Hessian nilpotent polynomials

evidence.quote: A polynomial or formal power series P(z) is said to be HN (Hessian nilpotent) if its Hessian matrix Hes P := ( d^2P / dz_i dz_j ) are nilpotent.

Conjecture 1.1. (Vanishing Conjecture) Let Delta := Sum_{i=1}^n D_i^2 be the Laplace operator of C[z]. Then, for any HN polynomial P(z) (of homogeneous of degree d = 4), Delta^m P^{m+1}(z) = 0 when m >> 0.

accepted.question_text: Suppose P(z) is a formal power series in C[[z]] with order at least 2 and with (Hes P)(0) nilpotent, so that its inversion pair Q(z) is defined by the symmetric formal map F(z) = z - grad P(z) and its formal inverse G(z) = z + grad Q(z). If P is self-inverting, meaning that its inversion pair satisfies Q(z) = P(z), must every self-inverting polynomial or formal power series automatically be Hessian nilpotent?
accepted.context_brief: whether self-inverting series are automatically Hessian nilpotent

evidence.quote: Definition 4.1. A formal power series P(z) in C[[z]] with o(P(z)) >= 2 and (Hes P)(0) nilpotent is said to be self-inverting if its inversion pair Q(z) = P(z).
Open Problem 4.8. (a) Decide whether or not all self-inverting polynomials or formal power series are HN.

accepted.question_text: Classify all self-inverting polynomials and formal power series whose inversion pair equals the series itself, and in particular classify all such examples that are Hessian nilpotent.
accepted.context_brief: classification of Hessian nilpotent self-inverting series

evidence.quote: It is unknown if all HN self-inverting polynomials or formal power series can be obtained by the construction above. More generally, we believe the following open problem is worth investigating.
Open Problem 4.8. (b) Classify all (HN) self-inverting polynomials and formal power series.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Hessian nilpotent formal power series P(z) in C[[z]] that is not a polynomial and for which the Vanishing Conjecture fails? Equivalently, can one find a non-polynomial Hessian nilpotent formal power series over C such that the quantities Delta^m(P(z)^(m+1)) do not eventually vanish, or prove that no such example exists?
accepted.context_brief: possible failure of the vanishing conjecture for non-polynomial Hessian nilpotent series

evidence.quote: One interesting question is whether or not the VC fails (as the JC does) for any HN formal power series P(z) in C[[z]] but P(z) not in C[z]? To our best knowledge, no such counterexample has been known yet.
Open Problem 5.2. Find a HN formal power series P(z) in C[[z]] but P(z) not in C[z], if there are any, such that the VC fails for P(z).

accepted.question_text: Let P(z) be a formal power series in C[[z]] with order o(P(z)) >= 2. If the sequence Delta^m(P(z)^m) eventually vanishes, meaning Delta^m(P(z)^m) = 0 for all sufficiently large m, must P(z) be Hessian nilpotent?
accepted.context_brief: eventual vanishing of Delta^m P^m versus Hessian nilpotency

evidence.quote: A polynomial or formal power series P(z) is said to be HN (Hessian nilpotent) if its Hessian matrix Hes P := ( d^2P / dz_i dz_j ) are nilpotent.
Conjecture 6.4. Let P(z) in C[[z]] with o(P(z)) >= 2. If Delta^m P^m(z) = 0 for m >> 0, then P(z) is HN.

accepted.question_text: Let P(z) be a homogeneous harmonic polynomial of degree d >= 2 written in the form P(z) = sum_{i=1}^k h alpha_i, z i^d with isotropic vectors alpha_i in C^n, and define the graph G(P) to have vertex set {1, 2, ..., k} with an edge between i and j exactly when <alpha_i, alpha_j> is nonzero. What necessary or sufficient conditions on this labeled graph G(P) ensure that P(z) is Hessian nilpotent?

evidence.quote: We fix a homogeneous harmonic polynomial P(z) in C[z] of degree d >= 2, and assume that P(z) is given by Eq. (8.2) for some alpha_i in X(C^n) (1 <= i <= k).
The set of vertices of G(P) will be the set of positive integers [k] := {1, 2, . . . , k}. The vertices i and j of G(P) are connected by an edge iff <alpha_i, alpha_j> != 0.
Open Problem 8.4. (a) Find some necessary or sufficient conditions on the (labeled) graph G(P) such that the homogeneous harmonic polynomial P(z) is HN.

accepted.question_text: In the same graph-theoretic setting for a homogeneous harmonic polynomial P(z) and its associated graph G(P), what necessary or sufficient conditions on the labeled graph G(P) guarantee that the Vanishing Conjecture holds for the homogeneous Hessian nilpotent polynomial P(z)?
accepted.context_brief: graph-theoretic criteria for the vanishing conjecture

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8.4. (b) Find some necessary or sufficient conditions on the (labeled) graph G(P) such that the VC holds for the homogeneous HN polynomial P(z).
